notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: God is the light of the heavens and the earth.

The similitude of His light is like a niche with a lamp in it, the lamp in a glass, the glass like a bright star, lit from a blessed olive tree that is neither eastern nor western, whose oil would almost give light even if no fire touched it: light upon light.
God guides to His light whom He wills, and God strikes the similitudes for people, and God knows all things.
In houses that God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered, there is glorifying of Him in the mornings and the evenings.
There are men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God, from establishing the prayer and from giving zakat; they fear a day on which hearts and sight are turned about.
The ayah states the purpose: that God may reward them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty; and God provides for whom He wills without account.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah says that God is the light of the heavens and the earth, and gives a similitude of His light as a niche with a lamp in a glass [c1][c2]. The next ayat speak of houses in which God is remembered and of men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from remembering Him [c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
God is the light of the heavens and the earth [c1]. The similitude of His light is like a niche with a lamp in it, the lamp in a glass, the glass like a bright star [c2]. The lamp is lit from a blessed olive tree that is neither eastern nor western, whose oil would almost give light even if no fire touched it: light upon light [c2]. God guides to His light whom He wills, and God strikes the similitudes for people, and God knows all things [c3].

In houses that God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered, there is glorifying of Him in the mornings and the evenings [c4]. There are men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God, from establishing the prayer and from giving zakat [c5]. They fear a day on which hearts and sight are turned about [c5]. The ayah states the purpose: that God may reward them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty [c6]. God provides for whom He wills without account [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The similitude is built from named parts: a niche, a lamp, a glass, a star and an olive tree, and it ends with the words light upon light [c2]. The ayah then says that God guides to His light whom He wills [c3]. The ayat that follow speak of houses and of men, and the Arabic opens them with the word in, so that they can be read with the niche or as a new sentence [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: God is the light of the heavens and the earth [c1]. The ayah gives a picture of His light as a niche with a lamp in a glass, and the glass is like a bright star [c2]. God guides to His light whom He wills [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah speaks of the light of God and then of those who remember Him in houses [c1][c4][c5]. Another reading is that the picture of light upon light is followed by the statement that God guides to His light whom He wills [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the niche, the lamp, the glass and the tree each stand for beyond what the ayah says.
- Not established: whose light the pronoun in 'His light' (nurihi) is read as; it is read as God's light, and some readings take it as the light of the believer. This draft keeps God's light.
- The attachment of 24:36 to the picture of the niche is read in more than one way; this draft treats the houses as a separate statement.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later commentary identifies the houses, the men and the blessed tree with particular buildings, people and trees; this draft does not repeat or vouch for them.
- The ayah itself says that God strikes the similitudes (24:35).
- The phrase kawkab durri is rendered 'a bright star'; a scholar may prefer another wording.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: the reports that later commentary links to 24:35-38, to be found, graded by a named grader and linked by a scholar.
The wordings to check first: the attachment of 24:36, the pronoun in 'His light', and kawkab durri.
